haiku-low.q1: No session. The server creates a login_challenges row, sets the mfa cookie, and shows the code prompt.
haiku-low.q2: As soon as setup is confirmed with a valid code, which moves the pending secret into user_totp. Sign-in ignores pending secrets until then.
haiku-low.q3: The recovery code is burned and the challenge deleted in one transaction, then start_session runs. Email is queued afterwards; sign-in does not depend on it.
haiku-low.q4: A 5th wrong entry or 5 minutes elapsed. The challenge and mfa cookie are deleted and the user is redirected to the password form.
haiku-low.q5: Confirming setup deletes all other sessions of the user, keeping only the current session.
haiku-low.q6: No. The last_step atomic update rejects reuse. Tolerance is one 30-second time step either side of the server clock.
haiku-low.q7: One transaction moves the pending secret into user_totp, sets last_step, replaces recovery codes, deletes other sessions and the pending row. On failure it rolls back fully.
haiku-low.q8: In the login_challenges table, with the browser holding an httponly mfa cookie. Removed on success, the 5th wrong entry, or expiry.
haiku-low.q9: Active secret, confirmed_at and last_step are in user_totp; pending secret in totp_pending; recovery code hashes in recovery_codes. 2FA is on when user_totp has confirmed_at set.
haiku-low.q10: The active authenticator stays in force during replacement, since the pending secret is inert. Cancelling returns to On with the old authenticator unchanged.
haiku-low.q11: The server tries the input as an authenticator code first, then as a recovery code. Wrong recovery codes count, as any wrong entry increments failures toward 5.
haiku-low.q12: Not designed. It is an open product decision with no transition, endpoint or code path, so such a user cannot sign in until product decides.

sonnet.q1: Only a challenge: a login_challenges row plus an mfa cookie and the code prompt. No session is created and start_session is not called.
sonnet.q2: Once the user confirms it with a valid code. Until then the pending secret is inert and sign-in ignores it. Confirmation creates the user_totp row with confirmed_at set, which is what turns 2FA On.
sonnet.q3: The recovery code is burned (single-use) and the challenge is deleted in one transaction. After commit, enqueue_email(user_id, "recovery_code_used", {remaining}) is called, then start_session gives a normal session. Sign-in does not depend on the email: it does not wait for it, and a failed send never affects sign-in.
sonnet.q4: The 5th wrong entry, or 5 minutes elapsing from challenge creation (retries do not extend it). The challenge and mfa cookie are deleted and the user is redirected to the password form to start again from the password. A missing, unknown or expired challenge also goes back to the password form.
sonnet.q5: On confirm, every other session of the user is deleted (DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id = $u AND token_hash <> sha256($current)). The current session stays.
sonnet.q6: No. A code is accepted only if its step is greater than last_step, enforced by an atomic UPDATE ... WHERE last_step < $s; zero rows changed means reject. Tolerance is the current 30-second step and one step either side of the server clock.
sonnet.q7: In one transaction: the pending secret moves into user_totp (overwriting the old secret on replace), last_step is set to the confirming code's step, all old recovery codes are deleted and 10 new hashed ones inserted, all other sessions of the user are deleted, and the pending row is deleted. The 10 plaintext codes are returned once. If the transaction fails it rolls back completely: the user stays as before and no codes are shown.
sonnet.q8: In the login_challenges table (token_hash PK, user_id, created_at, expires_at = created_at + 5 min, failures). The browser refers to it by the mfa cookie (httponly, secure, SameSite=Lax, max_age 300), made with new_token(32) and stored as a hash. It is removed on successful second factor, on the 5th wrong entry, or on expiry. The mfa cookie is never accepted as a session.
sonnet.q9: Secret: user_totp.secret_sealed, sealed with seal(). Enrolment status: confirmed_at in user_totp, and unconfirmed secrets sit in totp_pending (sealed). Replay protection: user_totp.last_step. Recovery codes: recovery_codes table (code_hash, used_at), hashes only. 2FA is On if the user has a user_totp row with confirmed_at set. No row means Off.
sonnet.q10: The old authenticator stays active and required, because the new secret sits in totp_pending, which sign-in never reads. A wrong code leaves the replacement pending and the old one active. If abandoned or cancelled, nothing changes. The state returns to On with the old secret (the doc does not describe a timeout or cleanup of the pending row).
sonnet.q11: The server tries the input first as an authenticator code, then as a recovery code. A recovery code is accepted only if it matches an unused one. The document does not state whether wrong recovery codes are counted separately. It says a wrong entry increments failures, with the 5th wrong entry discarding the challenge. That wording suggests any wrong entry counts, but this is not stated explicitly for recovery codes.
sonnet.q12: None. This is an open product decision. LostPhoneNoCodes is a deliberate dead end with no transition, endpoint or table designed. Until product decides, such a user cannot sign in.
